task.description:
Write the test spec and test code for REQ-372, per WF-02 Step 3's procedure (docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md) and .claude/agents/test-designer.md. Scope test first: this requirement has real application-executable surface (a new module, lib/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation.ex, plus modified call sites in lib/letflow/definitions.ex) -- proceed to the full procedure (do not skip to RELEASE-VALIDATOR).

You are on branch feature/WF02-REQ372-20260921 -- verify with git branch --show-current, pull if needed.

Write test/specs/REQ-372.md (requirement text, test cases, why each exists) and test code under test/letflow/ (test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_test.exs for the new module's own unit tests, plus additions to test/letflow/definitions_test.exs -- or a new test file if that suits better, your call -- for the call-site integration tests against activate/2 and validate_definition_graph/2). Read lib/letflow/design/req372-semantic-decision-rule-validation.md for the exact function signatures and semantics you're testing against, and read the actual implementation in lib/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation.ex and lib/letflow/definitions.ex directly (not just the design -- the design describes intent, the implementation is what actually runs).

Every one of the 10 acceptance criteria in this handoff's task.acceptance_criteria must have at least one test case that would fail if the behavior were violated -- map each one explicitly in test/specs/REQ-372.md. In particular, these are NOT optional and each needs its own clearly-named test:
1. Undeclared-variable-reference violation naming the exact typed variable name and the step/edge it belongs to.
2. That violation's suggested nearest declared field name for a clear one-typo case: 'cusotmer_name' when 'customer_name' is declared -- assert the exact suggested name appears in the violation message.
3. Non-comparable type-pair violation, at minimum numeric/money vs text/string.
4. BOTH violation classes appearing together from a SINGLE validation call when a definition has one of each -- assert both violations are present in one result, not two separate calls.
5. A definition with zero semantic violations validates cleanly -- including a test that starts from the broken definition in test 4, corrects BOTH violations, and re-validates clean in the same test (proving the fix path, not just a fresh clean fixture).
6. THE RE-RUN-NOT-CACHED TEST (this is the one most likely to be under-tested -- design it carefully): call the release/promotion submission path (activate/2, per the design) once when the definition and its VariableSchema are clean/valid; then CHANGE the underlying state between calls (e.g. mutate the VariableSchema to remove a field a condition now references, or change a field's declared type to make a previously-fine comparison now non-comparable) WITHOUT going through any cache-invalidation hook; call activate/2 (or whatever the actual submission path is) again and assert the SECOND call reflects the fresh, now-invalid state (i.e. it fails/blocks for the NEW reason) rather than reusing a stale/cached validation result from the first call. This proves AC6 mechanically, not just documentation-wise.
7. No test is required to prove the HUMAN_TASK-in-scope decision itself (that's a moduledoc/doc criterion, not a test), but do NOT write a test that accidentally implies HUMAN_TASK routing is covered.

Follow the existing property-test convention where the codebase already uses one for state-machine-adjacent logic (check test/letflow/definitions_test.exs and test/letflow/definitions/graph_test.exs for existing style/fixture patterns and match them -- per-test unique data, no shared hardcoded IDs, no wall-clock/unseeded-randomness dependence, tests self-sufficient and not dependent on execution order).

Do NOT write or run mix test yourself in a way that substitutes for TEST-RUNNER's own step -- your job is to write correct, complete tests; TEST-RUNNER runs them next. You MAY do a local sanity compile/run to confirm your own tests aren't obviously broken, but the formal run is Step 4's job.

Claim the handoff (status IN_PROGRESS), write the tests, then set status COMPLETED with a genuine first-hand result. next_action on PASS: "Route to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR". Do not touch created_at/started_at. Commit all new/changed test files plus the updated handoff, push to origin/feature/WF02-REQ372-20260921. Never push to main, never touch web/.
acceptance_criteria: a definition whose EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY edge condition references a variable name absent from the definition's declared VariableSchema fields produces a violation naming the exact typed variable name and the step/edge it belongs to, proven by a test

that violation's message includes a suggested nearest declared field name, computed by a real string-distance measure (not a placeholder or first-alphabetical fallback), proven by a test with a clear one-typo case (e.g. 'cusotmer_name' when 'customer_name' is declared)

a definition comparing two operands of declared VariableSchema types this requirement records as non-comparable (at minimum: a numeric/money type against a text/string type) produces a violation, proven by a test; the comparable/non-comparable type-pair table is stated explicitly in the moduledoc, not left implicit

a definition with two independent broken rules (one field-existence violation, one type-compatibility violation) produces BOTH violations in a single validation call, proven by a test -- the author is never required to fix one to discover the other
a definition with zero semantic violations validates cleanly, proven by a test, including after both of the above violations are corrected in the same test

the semantic validation pass re-runs in full (not from a cached prior result) at the definition's actual release/promotion submission call path, proven by a test that changes the underlying VariableSchema or expression state between an earlier clean validation and the submission call, and asserts the submission call reflects the fresh state

whether a HUMAN_TASK routing/assignment-by-field mechanism is in scope for this requirement is stated explicitly in the moduledoc with the reasoning, not left for a reader to infer from what tests do or don't cover
git diff shows lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex unmodified, or if modified, modified only in ways that add no token/operator/builtin -- state which, per REQ-288's precedent
no file under web/ is modified by this requirement
mix letflow.check passes, with real output quoted
